transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Rajesh (CTO - Velaris), Emily (Head of Security), Samir (Infra), Olga (PM)

Summary: Short POC scoping focused on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency constraints for EU/US, egress controls, and benchmark/success criteria for a 4-week pilot. Agreed to run an initial latency+throughput benchmark and validate private connectivity.

00:00:04 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, and then Diego will walk through the network options and what we need for the POC.
00:00:18 - Rajesh: Sounds good, thanks. We're mostly trying to understand the networking tradeoffs and restrictions for patient data, so egress and region residency are big for us.
00:00:30 - Diego: Cool, I'll cover VPC peering vs PrivateLink, also talk about our private control plane option — for Velaris you'll likely want PrivateLink if you want no routing of traffic over the public internet. VPC peering is simpler but has some routing and cross-account limits.
00:01:05 - Emily: Just to be explicit, our compliance team requires data to remain in the EU for EU patients and we need audit logs for all requests. Also, customer-managed keys.
00:01:20 - Lina: We support KMS integrations and we produce audit logs. For residency, we can pin model endpoints to region or run Private deployment in your VPC. For hosted private networking we can peer to your account in eu-west-1 or set up PrivateLink in your account.
00:01:50 - Samir: If we do peering, do we need to NAT? What's the egress cost flow? We don't want traffic traversing public subnets.
00:02:05 - Diego: With peering traffic stays inside the cloud backbone, no internet egress. PrivateLink exposes an endpoint in your VPC and we connect via ENIs — that also avoids internet egress. Costs differ: PrivateLink has endpoint hours + data processing, peering is just data transfer. We'll send estimates.
00:02:40 - Olga: Timeline-wise, we want a pilot before end of April. Ideally two-week smoke + two-week load/quality benchmarking.
00:02:55 - Maya: That aligns with our typical POC: week 0 config and network setup, week 1 smoke testing and small latency benchmarks, week 2 full throughput runs and quality evals.
00:03:12 - Rajesh: Success criteria: p50 latency < 150ms for single-turn prompts up to 1k tokens, p95 < 400ms, throughput of 80 QPS sustained for 10s bursts, and cost per 1k tokens under $0.18 — that's our internal target. Also accuracy/regression checks on our clinical prompts.
00:03:44 - Diego: Good, we'll map that out. For throughput we need to size batchers and GPUs; can you share expected RPS and average context length?
00:03:58 - Rajesh: Current load is small: 15 RPS average, peaks 90 RPS during morning surge. Average context 600 tokens, 95th up to 3k for some long form notes. We can cap long requests in the POC.
00:04:20 - Emily: On egress, our SOC requires that logs and token payloads do not leave region for EU patients. Can Redwood ensure per-customer regional isolation?
00:04:34 - Lina: Yes, we can pin endpoints and route traffic to region-specific capacity. For private deployments we can run an on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane; we'll include the region mapping in the network doc.
00:04:50 - Maya: For the benchmark plan: Diego, can you outline what we need from Velaris? We're thinking: account details for peering/PrivateLink, sample prompt set (redacted PHI), a small dataset for quality evals, and a timeslot for throughput runs.
00:05:10 - Diego: Yep. Also need CIDR ranges, preferred subnet for endpoints, and a security contact who can approve SG rules.
00:05:23 - Samir: We can provide CIDRs and a service account. We prefer PrivateLink to avoid cross-account routing policies, but if PrivateLink costs explode maybe peering is ok.
00:05:40 - Rajesh: What about regional failover? If eu-west-1 has capacity issues, can requests failover to another EU region or to US? We can't send EU patient data outside EU.
00:05:55 - Lina: We support region routing policies and can enforce hard residency — requests from EU tokens stay in eu-west-1 or another EU region you choose. We'll not failover to US for EU data. Fallback to another EU region is possible but needs prior consent.
00:06:18 - Emily: Audit logs: we need 13 months retention and ability to export to our SIEM.
00:06:26 - Diego: We can stream logs to your S3 or CloudWatch in the region, and provide API for exports. We'll include log retention/config options.
00:06:40 - Olga: On the benchmark specs, we also want to measure cold-start latencies for KV cache misses and end-to-end p95 including network overhead.
00:06:52 - Diego: We'll design runs for warm vs cold cache. For model selection, are you using any specific model family? That affects GPU choice.
00:07:05 - Rajesh: We're evaluating open models right now — leaning toward a 13B quantized variant for cost reasons, but we want a guardrail to switch to a 70B if quality drops.
00:07:20 - Diego: Ok; we'll include model variants and quantization plan. For the POC we'll provision a few GPU-backed variants and document expected token/sec and latencies per variant.
00:07:36 - Maya: Quick note — competitors: Rajesh mentioned Bedrock as something they're looking at, plus Anthropic. We'll surface comparative notes but focus on your constraints.
00:07:50 - Rajesh: Yeah we requested some pricing from Bedrock but it's unclear on private networking.
00:07:58 - Maya: Action items recap in a bit. Diego — can you walk through the network diagrams?
00:08:06 - Diego: Sure. [screen share description omitted - shared doc link: /shared/network/velaris-private-link-vs-peering.pdf] 00:08:22 - Diego: Slide 1 shows PrivateLink: Redwood hosts service behind NLB, a service consumer creates an Interface Endpoint; all traffic over AWS backbone with ENI in your subnets. Pros: no route table changes, VPC endpoint policies. Cons: per-hour endpoint costs.
00:08:47 - Diego: Slide 2 shows VPC peering: simpler connection, lower recurring endpoint costs, but some restrictions on transitive routing and cross-account. Also need to manage overlapping CIDRs.
00:09:05 - Samir: Overlap is a no-go for us right now; our account has many legacy ranges. We prefer PrivateLink.
00:09:15 - Emily: Does PrivateLink support mTLS? We require mutual TLS between our services and the endpoint.
00:09:22 - Lina: We support mTLS termination on our side and can accept client certs. We'll include cert flow.
00:09:35 - Rajesh: For benchmarks, how long to spin up the test env?
00:09:40 - Maya: Network setup typically 2-3 business days after we get CIDRs and permissions. Provisioning capacity for GPU-backed variants takes a day. So plan for week 0 networking, week 1 smoke/latency, week 2 throughput and quality.
00:09:58 - Olga: If we find quality regressions, what's the rollback plan?
00:10:05 - Diego: We can rollback to a previous model variant or route traffic to a hosted fallback. For POC we keep a shadow baseline and run A/B comparisons.
00:10:18 - Emily: Data retention of logs and payloads: do you store request payloads by default?
00:10:25 - Lina: We don't store payloads unless you opt into enhanced logging; we store minimal metadata for observability. If you need full payload retention for debugging we can set up region-limited S3 with lifecycle policies.
00:10:40 - Rajesh: For cost estimation, please include network egress and PrivateLink hourly costs.
00:10:47 - Maya: We'll include detailed line items in the estimate.
00:10:55 - Diego: One more technical note: if you plan to run long context (3k tokens), we recommend batch size tuning and possibly KV cache pinning. That changes latency vs throughput tradeoffs.
00:11:12 - Samir: We'll cap at 2k for the POC to keep runs consistent.
00:11:19 - Rajesh: Benchmarks we expect: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, model quality on 200 redacted clinical prompts, and memory/CPU on infra. Also measure any variability during spikes.
00:11:35 - Diego: We'll prepare a benchmark harness and share the runbook. It will include warm/cold, step-up load, and regression checks against your prompt set.
00:11:50 - Maya: Ok let's do a very quick recap and owners. Maya will send security docs and pricing by Monday. Diego will send benchmark plan and runbook. Samir will share CIDR/subnet and a service account. Emily to confirm residency requirements. We'll aim to start network setup by 2026-03-24.
00:12:18 - Rajesh: That timeline works. Anything else?
00:12:25 - Olga: Please include an estimated SLOs table in the docs so we can discuss with ops.
00:12:31 - Lina: We'll include expected p50/p95 numbers per model variant and recommended autoscale settings.
00:12:40 - Maya: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and set up the benchmark slot.
00:12:48 - Rajesh: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
